items.title: German researchers develop AI that predicts liquid properties

featured_image.name: New AI method accelerates liquid simulations - Universität Bayreuth

items.description:
Artificial intelligence is transforming how scientists study complex physical systems, with recent breakthroughs enabling faster and more accurate simulations of everything from liquid behavior to electron dynamics in water.

Researchers at the University of Bayreuth announced this week a new AI method that can significantly speed up the calculation of liquid properties. Published in the journal Physical Review Letters as an Editors' Suggestion, the approach predicts the chemical potential—a fundamental quantity for describing liquids in thermodynamic equilibrium—without requiring the computationally expensive algorithms traditionally used for such calculations.[1]

items.title: Nissan narrows operating loss forecast as turnaround gains traction

featured_image.name: Nissan eyes tapping hot Japan real estate market with HQ ...

items.description:
Nissan announced Thursday it expects a net loss of 650 billion yen ($4.2 billion) for fiscal year 2025 ending in March, as the Japanese automaker continues its sweeping turnaround effort under new leadership. The loss is driven primarily by non-cash charges tied to restructuring under the company's "Re:Nissan" recovery plan.[1][2][3]

The forecast marks a difficult but potentially stabilizing chapter for Japan's third-largest carmaker, which has been battered by an aging vehicle lineup, intensifying competition from Chinese rivals, and the financial impact of U.S. tariffs on imported vehicles.

items.title: EU leaders meet in Belgium to counter economic pressure from U.S. and China

featured_image.name: EU leaders meet to counter pressure from Russia, China and Trump

items.description:
European Union leaders gathered Thursday at the historic Alden Biesen castle in eastern Belgium for an informal retreat aimed at revitalizing the bloc's stagnating economy and forging a united response to mounting pressure from the United States, China, and Russia.

The summit, convened by European Council President António Costa, comes as the 27-member bloc grapples with U.S. President Donald Trump's tariff threats, Chinese export restrictions on critical minerals, and hybrid threats from Moscow. Former Italian Prime Ministers Mario Draghi and Enrico Letta have been invited to present updates on their landmark 2024 reports on EU competitiveness and the single market.[1][2][3]

items.title: Penn State team unveils light-powered computer to cut AI energy use

featured_image.name: Programmable photonic chip uses light to accelerate AI ...

items.description:
As artificial intelligence places unprecedented demands on the world's electricity supply, researchers at Penn State have developed a prototype computer that processes data using light instead of traditional circuitry, a breakthrough they say could slash the energy consumption of AI systems.

The optical computing device, detailed in a paper published Wednesday in the journal Science Advances, routes light through an "infinity mirror" like loop of tiny optical components, encoding data directly into beams of light and capturing the resulting patterns with a microscopic camera. The system can perform complex AI calculations faster and with far less energy than conventional electronic computing.[1][2]

items.title: US energy secretary vows 'dramatic' oil output boost in Venezuela

featured_image.name: Delcy Rodríguez receives the U.S. Secretary of Energy ...

items.description:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright arrived in Caracas on Wednesday for talks with Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez, marking the highest-ranking American energy official visit to the South American nation in nearly 30 years. The meeting at Miraflores Palace focused on revitalizing Venezuela's struggling oil sector and attracting foreign investment following the recent overthrow of Nicolás Maduro.

Wright promised a "dramatic increase" in Venezuelan oil, natural gas, and electricity production, according to France24. "I am convinced we will witness an extraordinary shift in the future of this nation," Wright told reporters after meeting with Rodríguez. The energy secretary said he and Rodríguez "had frank discussions about the substantial opportunities before us" as well as potential challenges.[1]

items.title: Asian stocks hit record high after US jobs beat expectations

featured_image.name: Asia stocks rise as Nikkei sets fresh record, dollar drops

items.description:
Asian equity markets surged to unprecedented levels on Thursday as stronger-than-expected U.S. employment data boosted optimism about the American economy while simultaneously dimming expectations for near-term Federal Reserve interest rate cuts. The dollar strengthened on the news, weighing on currencies including the Canadian dollar and limiting gains in precious metals.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index climbed 0.65% in Thursday trading, reaching a fresh all-time high and extending its gains for the first six weeks of 2026 to approximately 13%, according to Reuters. Shares in South Korea and Japan reached record levels during early trading, propelled by strength in the technology sector.[1][2]

items.title: DeepMind CEO predicts AI-driven 'golden era' within 15 years

featured_image.name: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis sees "watershed moment" for AI

items.description:
Demis Hassabis, the Nobel Prize-winning CEO of Google DeepMind, has predicted that artificial intelligence will usher in a "new golden era of discovery" within the next 10 to 15 years, transforming medicine, solving the energy crisis, and potentially enabling humanity to venture beyond Earth.

Speaking on the Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast with Fortune Editor-in-Chief Alyson Shontell, Hassabis described a vision of "radical abundance" where AI harnesses the scientific method to tackle humanity's most intractable problems.[1][2]

"In 10 to 15 years, we will enter a new golden age of discovery, akin to a new renaissance," Hassabis said. He predicted that "medicine will not resemble what it is today," with AI enabling personalized treatments and curing major diseases.[1]

items.title: Caribbean reef food chains shortened 70% in 7,000 years, study finds

featured_image.name: 7,000 years of change: How humans reshaped Caribbean coral ...

items.description:
Caribbean coral reef food chains have shortened by 60 to 70 percent compared to their prehistoric state, according to a study published today in Nature, revealing that human activities have fundamentally altered how energy flows through these ecosystems and increased their vulnerability to collapse.

An international team of researchers, led by scientists at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute and Boston College, compared modern Caribbean reefs with fossils from approximately 7,000 years ago found in Panama and the Dominican Republic. They discovered that fish have become 20 to 70 percent less functionally diverse, with species that once occupied distinct dietary niches now competing for the same limited resources.[1][2]

items.title: Bangladesh holds first election since 2024 uprising ousted Hasina

featured_image.name: Is BNP’s Tarique Rahman the change post-Hasina Bangladesh is looking for?

items.description:
Bangladesh heads to the polls on Thursday in its first national election since a student-led uprising toppled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August 2024. More than 127 million voters will cast ballots in 299 constituencies, choosing between the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and an alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, while Hasina's Awami League remains barred from participating.

The election will also feature a simultaneous referendum on the July Charter, a document proposing constitutional reforms including a 10-year lifetime cap for prime ministers and expanded presidential powers. Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate who has led the interim government since Hasina's ouster, urged voters on Monday to support the charter, saying a "yes" vote would build Bangladesh's future "in a more positive way."[1]

items.title: Russia launches 'massive' missile attack on Kyiv, killing one

featured_image.name: Kyiv hit by 'massive' Russian missile, drone attack ...

items.description:
The Ukrainian capital Kyiv came under a "massive" Russian missile attack early Thursday morning, with Mayor Vitali Klitschko reporting that residential and non-residential buildings on both sides of the Dnipro River were hit as explosions echoed throughout the city.

"A mass attack on the capital is still underway," Klitschko said on Telegram, announcing that emergency medical teams had been dispatched to respond to the assault. The attack killed one person and injured four others, including a 9-year-old child, in the Obolonskyi district, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service.[1][2][3][4][5]
